title: Silvering Bath
pages: Craft the controller from silver ingots, attuned quartz from the Resonance Infuser, one glass, two Drawn Copper Tubes from the Wire Drawing Bench, a mechanical Bourdon Pressure Gauge, a Bath Circulation Pump and Stainless Vessel Stock. Make four Stainless Vessel Charges from four steel billets and one chromium ingot, then fire each charge in the Kiln at 900 heat for 100 ticks. The chromium-bearing alloy stock resists corrosion from the aqueous bath; unlike a zinc surface coat, chromium is added to the steel itself. Composition and lifetime are abstracted. Place a water cauldron directly beneath the controller, iron bars directly against its east and west sides, and iron bars two blocks out to the north and to the south (leaving the north and south faces open for item ports). It is a tier-5 device: its Silvered Mirror is required to craft the Heliostat Etcher.

Two Drawn Copper Tubes connect the pump to the bath and return the solution; draw two tagged copper ingots at the Wire Drawing Bench to obtain both tubes. The original pierced shell and pressure rating are abstracted. Silver ingots cannot stand in for the tubes. The pump keeps the silvering solution moving over the work. Craft two Monel Pump Blanks from four nickel ingots, two copper ingots, a Sintered Bronze Bushing (shaft support), Compression Packing (stationary gland) and a Rotary Lip Seal (rotating splash barrier); ingot tags accept other mods' matching metals. Braid four string around charcoal for two packing rings; the Fiber Carder makes renewable string. Combine a second packing ring with leather, an iron nugget spring and Bearing Grease to form the lip seal; honeycomb wax mixed with clay supplies two early grease; Rendered Tallow from the later Prism Separator is an alternative. Loose packing cannot replace the finished lip seal. The Copper Hot Press finishes one blank into a Bath Circulation Pump over 240 ticks at 14 FE/t. Nickel-copper (Monel-type) alloys are chosen for their corrosion resistance in aqueous salt and acid service, simplified for this game. A plain cauldron cannot replace the pump in the controller. The press takes item input from above or sides, FE through its capability, and offers output below; configure faces in its menu. Craft the gauge with four copper ingots bent into a C-shaped tube around a glass pane and a redstone pointer; its dial shows a mechanical pressure indication on the recirculation loop. Use the gauge in the controller recipe beside the pump; glass alone cannot replace it. The dial is an assembly requirement, not a live pressure control or safety interlock.

Hold the substrate batch in your main hand and one coating ingot in your off hand, then right-click the formed controller. This loads one complete batch (the listed substrate count plus exactly one coating ingot) into the bath's buffer; nothing is coated instantly. The bath coats it over 40 ticks, then right-click with an empty hand to collect the product. A short batch, or one the full buffer cannot take, is refused and your items stay in hand. Without cauldron water or any iron bar (bars directly against the north or south face do not count) the bath will not run; an empty off hand only shows a hint. Coatings are item tags (forge:ingots/<metal>), so any mod's matching ingot works.

It runs 21 datapack silvering recipes, each with a different metal. Two glass and silver give two Silvered Mirrors; four glass and indium give tinted glass. Torches with aluminum or soul torches with titanium become lanterns. Six rails with palladium, ruthenium or osmium become powered, detector or activator rails. Redstone with nickel or rhodium becomes a compass or clock; stone pressure plates with lead or platinum become weighted plates. Chromium plates leather horse armor into iron horse armor, cobalt turns a leather chestplate into chainmail, germanium and an amethyst shard make a spyglass, tantalum and paper make a name tag, three leather and manganese make a saddle, gold gilds a carrot and zinc a melon slice. Vanadium restores a chipped anvil and molybdenum a damaged one. Hafnium coats a Filter Window Blank (two glass panes laminated around quartz) with a thin dielectric film, giving the Coated Interference Filter that the t7 Spectral Filter craft requires.

Automation: face a hopper or pipe into the open north side (or the top) and pull coated products from the open south side; sneak-right-click an empty hand on a face to cycle input, output or disabled (the south face starts as input, so switch it to output once). Input faces offer two slots: substrates go to the stock slot and coating ingots to a separate reagent slot, so one hopper carrying both is sorted automatically and neither slot accepts the other's items. A formed bath coats one buffered batch every 40 ticks, consuming the listed substrate count and one coating ingot; with no ingot buffered it waits. Stored stock, coating and product survive reload and drop if the bath is broken, and a drained cauldron or missing bar pauses the buffer. An empty-hand click collects the product; hand coating still works as described. When two recipes match, the lowest recipe id wins. JEI's Silvering category lists substrate counts, coating tags and outputs with the bath as catalyst.
